item.title: Planar cut-and-project sets with interval windows are bi-Lipschitz equivalent to lattices
item.description: arXiv:2611.26707v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every cut-and-project set in a plane in $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose window is a line segment is bi-Lipschitz equivalent to a lattice: if $V\subseteq\mathbb{R}^3$ is a plane which is not spanned by vectors in $\mathbb{Z}^3$, $x\in\mathbb{R}^3$, and $\sigma$ is a segment of any length which is transverse to $V$, then the set of points $v\in V$ with $v+x\in\sigma+\mathbb{Z}^3$ is bi-Lipschitz equivalent to $\mathbb{Z}^2$. For planes of Diophantine slope this is a theorem of Burago and Kleiner, and the point of the present paper is that no Diophantine condition on the plane is needed. We also show that the same conclusion holds when the window is a finite union of intervals. Together with the author's construction of a cut-and-project set in a plane in $\mathbb{R}^3$, with a compact window of countable boundary, which is not bi-Lipschitz equivalent to any lattice, this shows that for planes in $\mathbb{R}^3$ the answer to the bi-Lipschitz question depends on the shape of the window rather than on the Diophantine properties of the plane.
item.dc:creator: Alan Haynes

item.title: Improved perimeter bounds for Hausdorff approximation by convex polygons
item.description: arXiv:2611.27403v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate how closely a convex polygon with at most n vertices can approximate a plane convex body of given perimeter. For free approximation in the Euclidean Hausdorff metric we improve Popov's bound for every $n \geq 3$. We also improve his inscribed bound for every $n \geq 3$ and his circumscribed bound for $n = 3$. The common step is to join successive boundary contacts of the body and estimate the perimeter lost in passing to their convex hull.
item.dc:creator: Krishnendu Bhowmick, Kurt Klement Gottwald

item.title: Analytic Projective Finsler Metrics and Sprays
item.description: arXiv:2611.26859v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study projective Finsler metrics and sprays on an open subset $U$ of $R^n$. They are characterized by the Hamel equations \[ P_{x^m y^k}y^m=P_{x^k}, \] where $P=P(x, y)$ are function on $TU$ with positive homogeneity: $P(x, cy)= c (x,y)$, $c >0$. This is the Hilbert's Fourth problem in the regular case. We determine all solutions analytic in the base variable. We compare this local representation with earlier work on Hilbert's fourth problem and with the restricted Taylor expansions arising for projective Finsler metrics of constant flag curvature. We conclude with explicit nonlinear projective Finsler metrics and sprays on Euclidean space, including one-sided complete examples and a nonflat complete example.
item.dc:creator: Zhongmin Shen

item.title: Small spherical 7-designs in prime dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.26879v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For every prime $p\ge 29$, we construct an antipodal spherical $7$-design on $S^{p-1}$ with $42(p-1)(p+2)^2$ points. The construction uses eigenlines of finite Weil operators.
item.dc:creator: Andriy Bondarenko, Dmytro Mitin

item.title: Dimension-free estimates for covering functionals of simplices and $\ell_p$ balls
item.description: arXiv:2606.01082v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study \(\Gamma_{2^n}(K)\), the least positive number \(\gamma>0\) such that an \(n\)-dimensional convex body \(K\) can be covered by \(2^n\) translates of \(\gamma K\). For \(n\)-simplices \(\Delta_n\), we prove that \(\Gamma_{2^n}(\Delta_n)\), as a sequence in \(n\), tends to \(1/2\). For the cross-polytope \(B_1^n\), we show that \(\Gamma_{2^n}(B_1^n)\leq5/6\) holds for all \(n\geq2\), and that \(\limsup_{n\to\infty}\Gamma_{2^n}(B_1^n)\leq0.641\cdots\). Finally, we prove the existence of a constant \(\kappa_*<1\) such that \(\Gamma_{2^n}(B_p^n)\leq\kappa_*\) for all \(n\geq2\) and all \(p\in[1,\infty]\).
item.dc:creator: Feifei Chen, Chan He, Senlin Wu

item.title: New best-known coverings, packing-coverings and quantizers in low dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2609.30513v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct periodic point sets that improve the best known covering densities in dimensions six and seven, packing-covering constants in dimensions five, six, and seven, and normalized second moments in dimensions five and six. In dimension five, a set of the original family of Cohn-Kumar-Sch\"urmann has packing-covering constant $9/\sqrt{40}$, strictly below the proven optimum for the lattice case. All seven point sets belong to a two-parameter subfamily of a four-parameter generalization of the Cohn-Kumar-Sch\"urmann family.
item.dc:creator: Sven Ahrend, Mathieu Dutour Sikiri\'c

item.title: Banchoff Curvature and Realisation Moduli of Piecewise-Affine Arrangement Immersions
item.description: arXiv:2611.22976v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We compute the curvature concentrated on the flats of a piecewise-affine immersion of $\mathbb{R}^D$ into $\mathbb{R}^n$ creased along an affine hyperplane arrangement, and parametrise the immersions sharing its chamber metrics. Suppose every transverse crease cone is embedded (the positive-path-rank condition). Then the Gauss-Bonnet-Chern density of any convex coordinate-wise smoothing that is affine outside a compact transition zone reduces, on each transverse slice, to a Hafnian. This Hafnian integrates to Banchoff's critical-point curvature on each even-codimension flat. The curvature coincides with the Cheeger-M\"uller-Schrader density and equals an alternating sum of Gaussian orthant probabilities determined by Schur complements of the incident chamber metrics. In even dimension, under mild non-degeneracy, total vertex curvature equals the recession curvature at infinity and is unchanged when the walls are translated, even across multi-wall collisions. Under generic codimension-two intersections, realisations with prescribed chamber metrics form a compact rank-constrained spectrahedron of generic local dimension $\max(0,H-r(r+1)/2)$, where $r = \max(0,D+H-n)$. At minimal target dimension the given immersion is the unique realisation preserving orientation across each single wall, and a positive semidefinite stress matrix certifies universal rigidity.
item.dc:creator: William Nelson

item.title: Super Guarding and Dark Rays in Art Galleries
item.description: arXiv:2404.04613v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We explore an Art Gallery variant where each point of a polygon must be seen by k guards, and guards cannot see through other guards. Surprisingly, even covering convex polygons under this variant is not straightforward. For example, covering every point in a triangle k=4 times (a 4-cover) requires 5 guards, and achieving a 10-cover requires 12 guards. Our main result is tight bounds on k-covering a convex polygon of n vertices, for all k and n. The proofs of both upper and lower bounds are nontrivial. We also obtain bounds for simple polygons, leaving tight bounds an open problem.
item.dc:creator: MIT CompGeom Group, Hugo A. Akitaya, Erik D. Demaine, Adam Hesterberg, Anna Lubiw, Jayson Lynch, Joseph O'Rourke, Frederick Stock

item.title: An exceptional set of uniformly spread Kakutani tilings of the line
item.description: arXiv:2512.23079v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The $\alpha$-Kakutani substitution rule splits the unit interval into two subintervals of lengths alpha and $1 - \alpha$, for a fixed $\alpha \in (0,1)$. A simple inflation-substitution procedure produces tilings of the real line and their associated Delone sets. We show that there are precisely five distinct values of $\min(\alpha, 1 - \alpha)$ for which these sets are uniformly spread, meaning that they are a bounded displacement of a lattice. The proof of this surprising fact combines the construction and analysis of a related family of primitive substitution tilings, Solomon's criterion for uniform spreadness, and a classification of Pisot-Vijayaraghavan polynomials.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Yotam Smilansky. An exceptional set of uniformly spread Kakutani tilings of the line. Discrete and Continuous Dynamical Systems 61 (2027), p. 105565
item.dc:creator: Yotam Smilansky

item.title: Affine balancing of complex dilatations: affine invariants and optimal distortion of harmonic quasiconformal mappings
item.description: arXiv:2609.37606v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Target real-affine postcomposition induces a disk automorphism on the complex dilatation of orientation-preserving planar harmonic mapping. Motivated by the lack of intrinsic distortion measures for real-affine orbits, we introduce the affine circumradius, affine diameter, and affine circumcenter from the hyperbolic geometry of the dilatation range. The affine circumradius is the logarithm of the minimal value of the maximal differential distortion over the real-affine orbit, and the affine circumcenter describes minimizers up to Euclidean similarity. For non-constant dilatation, at most two or three contact points determine the minimal enclosing hyperbolic disk. We prove sharp two-sided radius-diameter bounds, with equalities realized by globally univalent harmonic quasiconformal mappings. Each orbit admits a canonical balanced representative, for which we derive a sharp norm bound for the gap between the harmonic pre-Schwarzian derivative and that of its analytic part. This bound exhibits quadratic small-dilatation asymptotics, and the balanced representative achieves the minimal dilatation parameter over the real-affine orbit.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Gang Wang, Deguang Zhong

item.title: Decoupling and Tail Laws for Small-Order Metric-Valued Nonlocal Energies: A Structural View of the Maz'ya--Shaposhnikova Formula
item.description: arXiv:2610.01958v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a measure-theoretic framework for small-order limits of nonlocal energies with metric-valued maps. For globally $L^p$ maps, we consider interaction measures whose marginals have uniformly bounded $L^\infty$ densities $a_\alpha$ and $b_\alpha$. If these densities converge weakly-* to $a_\infty$ and $b_\infty$, the normalized energies converge to the $L^p$ energy weighted by $a_\infty+b_\infty$ if and only if the interaction measures escape every bounded rectangle. For maps that are only locally $L^p$, we introduce target laws describing the distribution of the values sampled at infinity. Convergence of their $p$-distance profiles yields the limiting interaction energy for every $1\leq p<\infty$ and arbitrary Polish targets, with integrated $p$-Wasserstein convergence as a sufficient criterion. The arguments include the endpoint $p=1$ and require no linear structure on the target space. Applications include directional and anisotropic Maz'ya--Shaposhnikova formulas, a Bernoulli-law interpretation of fractional perimeters, and an Abelian principle for heat-semigroup energies.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Pinamonti

item.title: Singular Atiyah Configurations
item.description: arXiv:2610.33090v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct arbitrarily large configurations of distinct points in Euclidean three-space with linearly dependent Atiyah polynomials, including planar configurations. The configurations consist of two coaxial cyclic orbits and axial points. We also obtain analogous configurations in hyperbolic three-space. In particular, our results disprove Atiyah's conjecture on configurations of points and its hyperbolic analogue.
item.dc:creator: Jan Eickhoff
